sources.entry: QuietSpeech - Push-to-talk dictation for Apple silicon that types into any app using Apple's on-device speech recognition and Apple Intelligence, with no API key. Paid app; source under GPLv3 (macOS 26+).

summary.one_liner: QuietSpeech is a push-to-talk dictation and text-editing app for Apple silicon Macs that types cleaned-up speech into any app using Apple's on-device speech recognition.
summary.what_it_does: Hold the Fn key, speak, and release; the cleaned-up transcript is inserted at the cursor in whatever app is active. Apple's on-device recognizer transcribes while the key is held and an overlay shows the live transcript. Filler words, false starts and missing punctuation are cleaned up before insertion. Selecting text and speaking an instruction such as "make it shorter" rewrites the selection, and saying "generate" followed by a request inserts a drafted text. In editors and terminals, AI polish is skipped and spoken flags like "dash dash watch" become flags. Users can add vocabulary terms for the recognizer and optionally connect OpenAI, Groq, Ollama, or a custom endpoint instead of on-device cleanup.
use_cases: dictate text into any Mac app
dictate code flags and commands in a terminal
notable: Fully on-device transcription and cleanup by default, with no account or telemetry
Optional providers: OpenAI, Groq, Ollama, or a custom endpoint
Code-aware mode that skips AI polish and converts spoken flags in editors and terminals
Includes polish-bench and speech-bench scripts for scoring cleanup and comparing recognizers on your own audio
Falls back to rules-based cleanup when Apple Intelligence is off
caveats: Requires macOS 26 or later and an Apple silicon Mac
Apple Intelligence must be enabled for AI cleanup, editing and generating; otherwise only rules-based cleanup is used
Paid app: the notarized download and license keys come from quietspeech.app; source is GPLv3
Ad-hoc builds without a Developer ID certificate make macOS ask for permissions again after every rebuild
